title: A Trail for the Horizon
premise: Yara Brightwater has run cargo up the Serapine River for twelve years, keeping the world at oar's length after a betrayal she refuses to name. When a government survey team vanishes above the Gorge of Nine Bends, leaving their instruments stacked neatly and no footprints, colonial officials conscript her leaking boat and her knowledge to find them before the monsoon swells and the concession permits expire. With a taciturn stranger named Ede who claims to have seen the team last, Yara navigates rising water, sabotage, and the discovery that the survey's true purpose is to displace the river communities she secretly considers her own people. The vanishing was staged by a surveyor who defected to protect the villages, and Yara must choose between delivering him for her permit—and her boat—and burning her papers to stand with the river folk, ending with her scuttling her own vessel to block the survey convoy and finding belonging on shore.
about_author: Paloma Vasquez spent six years working seasonal freight runs on inland waterways before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people whose livelihoods are measured in miles, weather, and other people's paperwork.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A routine cargo run down the low Serapine establishes her mastery of the river, her decaying boat the Kestrel, and her deliberate solitude—she pays everyone, owes no one, belongs nowhere. A clerk at the last dock posts notice that survey teams are moving upstream. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Officials at Fort Merrow conscript the Kestrel: a survey party vanished above the gorge, leaving instruments arranged in perfect rows and no tracks. The penalty for refusal is revocation of her trading permit. She meets Ede, a gaunt stranger who claims he guided the team and escaped alone. Emotional beat: resentment hardening into reluctant duty.

chapters.title: The Stranger's Silence
chapters.summary: Ede's POV. Upstream through narrowing channels, Ede watches Yara read the water like scripture while hiding what he knows: the surveyor Voss didn't vanish—he walked into the hills. Ede lies by omission, torn between self-preservation and growing respect. First signs of sabotage: someone has slashed a fuel line. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Storm clouds stack over the highlands; the Kestrel takes on water faster than the pumps can answer. They shelter in a stilt village where children know Yara by an old nickname she thought buried, revealing she once belonged here before her betrayal. The villagers warn the survey means eviction. Emotional beat: the ache of a home she exiled herself from.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Measure
chapters.summary: Ede's POV. Examining the abandoned gear, Ede realizes the 'survey' maps village land for concession boundaries, not the river channel. He confesses partially to Yara: Voss fled rather than sign the displacement order. An official aboard, Inspector Crane, grows suspicious and begins cataloguing the crew. Emotional beat: the cost of half-truths compounding.

chapters.title: Nine Bends Rising
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Racing the monsoon front through the gorge, they find Voss's trail and then Voss himself, half-starved, guarding evidence of the concession's forged boundaries. Crane attempts an arrest; a flash flood separates the party, sweeping the Kestrel toward a strainer. Yara saves Crane against her own instinct. Emotional beat: survival forcing strange loyalties.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Stranded on high ground, Voss tells Yara the whole design: the permits expire in nine days, and whoever holds the signed boundary map holds the villages' fate. He offers it to her—not as cargo, but as a choice. Crane, humbled by the rescue, wavers between career and conscience. Emotional beat: power revealed as something that can be handed off.

chapters.title: Crane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Crane's POV. Back aboard the patched Kestrel, Crane calculates: deliver Voss and the map, receive promotion and a share of concession fees—or bury his career. Sabotage is traced to his own junior officer, bought by the concession company, showing how far its corruption reaches. Crane quietly switches sides. Emotional beat: corruption exposed, integrity chosen late but chosen.

chapters.title: The Scuttling
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. At the confluence where the survey convoy waits for the expired-permit deadline, Yara runs the Kestrel aground across the channel and opens her own seacocks, sinking her boat to block the convoy's passage while Crane delivers the forged-boundary evidence to the arriving magistrate. Twelve years of miles go under the brown water. Emotional beat: grief and liberation in one breath.

chapters.title: A Trail for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Weeks later, the concessions voided, Yara stands in the stilt village that still remembers her name, helping raise a new dock. Voss teaches reading; Ede repairs boats beside her; the river keeps its moods without her. She measures life now in seasons and neighbors instead of miles. Emotional beat: belonging earned at the price of everything she used to be.
